claims.claim: F3 fix: extractor resolves target_entity from the JPA field declaration and output.ts renders both endpoints using the resolved entity's table_name
claims.evidence: entities-full.json shows target_entity populated for all 3 relationships (User, Order, Role). database-mapping.md emits 'users ||--o{ orders' (resolved to table_name 'orders' from entity 'Order') with no '_rel' placeholder. Both halves of the F3 fix are demonstrable in outputs.

claims.claim: Role is detected as a relationship target even though no @Entity Role class exists in the fixtures directory
claims.evidence: fixtures/jpa/ contains only Order.java, User.java, UserRepository.java — no Role.java. Yet User.many_to_many.target_entity='Role' (from @ManyToMany List<Role> roles). The Mermaid output renders 'users }o--o{ role' using a lowercased class name as the node label, since no extracted Role entity provides a table_name.

claims.claim: Both @Table(name) and schema attributes are parsed correctly by the JPA profile
claims.evidence: User.java @Table(name="users", schema="public") -> {table_name:'users', schema:'public'}. Order.java @Table(name="orders") (no schema) -> {table_name:'orders', schema:''}. Both parsed as expected.

suggestions.assertion: Every relationship in detected-entities.json has a non-empty target_entity that names another extracted class — no blank target_entity strings
suggestions.reason: The assertion's literal subject (detected-entities.json) does not carry a target_entity field — the public orm_detect.js JSON contract only serializes the relationship type string array. The executor had to manually import extractEntities() and dump to entities-full.json to satisfy the intent. Either (a) tighten orm_detect.js's --output-json to include target_entity per relationship, or (b) rewrite the assertion to name the artifact that actually carries it (e.g. 'Mermaid edges in database-mapping.md resolve to real table names at both endpoints, never a lowercased class name or a _rel placeholder'). As written, a buggy agent that emits detected-entities.json with just type strings (exactly what happens today) technically cannot fail this assertion — but also cannot prove it passes.

The many_to_many Role relationship silently falls back to a lowercased class name ('role') as the Mermaid node label because no Role entity was extracted (Role.java is not in the fixtures). The edge 'users }o--o{ role' creates a phantom node that is neither a real extracted table nor a '_rel' placeholder — so it passes the '_rel' assertion, but it is still a dangling reference. Consider an assertion like 'every Mermaid node in the erDiagram block matches a table_name from detected-entities.json.entities[].table_name' to catch this class of bug.

suggestions.assertion: @Table(name) maps to table names 'users' and 'orders' respectively; User also carries schema='public' from @Table(schema="public")
suggestions.reason: This assertion is satisfied by the JSON schema field, but doesn't verify that the schema propagates into the Mermaid diagram or the markdown table. The markdown shows 'public.users' in the Entity-Table Mapping table (good), but the Mermaid block uses bare 'users' with no schema prefix — worth explicitly asserting the intended behavior on each surface.

eval_feedback.overall: All 8 assertions pass with solid evidence. The F3 fix (target_entity resolution -> real table_name in Mermaid endpoints) is verifiably correct. Main eval gap: assertion #4 names the wrong artifact (detected-entities.json doesn't carry target_entity in its public contract), and the phantom-node check only catches '_rel' placeholders, missing the lowercased-classname fallback that still leaks when a relationship's target class is outside the scanned fixture set.
